newsitem.title: UK: Britain fails to reach HK agreement with China.
newsitem.headline: Britain fails to reach HK agreement with China.

text.p: Britain and China said on Friday they had failed to reach agreement on key areas in talks to hammer out details of Hong Kong's handover on June 30.
Hugh Davies, a senior British representative at the talks, said he was disappointed and frustrated that, after five years of talks with China, all details had not yet been worked out.

"Although we have reached some agreements this week, there are still a number of important matters where consensus is elusive," said Davies after the Anglo-Chinese Joint Liaison Group (JLG), the diplomatic body handling Hong Kong's return to China, wound up three days of talks in London.
The Chinese delegation, meanwhile, blamed Britain for the lack of progress.

"The Chinese side has made the greatest possible effort to accommodate the concerns of the British side, but the British side is still adopting disappointing delaying tactics and trying to establish linkage between unrelated issues," said China's ambassador to London, Zhao Jihua, who heads the Chinese delegation.
Two key areas of dispute remain the "right of abode" concerning citizenship rights and the posting of Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) troops in Hong Kong before the handover date.

"Perhaps most disappointingly, we have failed to resolve our differences on right of abode," Davies said. "This is frustrating, because after almost five years of discussions, we are now in a large measure of agreement on almost all the substantive issues involved in this complex subject. But we need to close the remaining gaps."
Zhao said the right of abode was for China to decide. "It falls within the internal affairs of China," he said.
On an advance guard of Chinese troops, Davies said the two sides had narrowed their differences but had been unable to reach agreement.
"Britain has long taken the position that some advance parties are a good idea," he said. The problems lie in the size of those parties and the timing of their arrival.
Davies stressed that some points of contention had been cleared up at the talks including agreements on legislation for mutual legal assistance and the transfer of sentenced persons.
He said aviation agreements had been reached with the United States and Indonesia bringing to 20 the total number of accords now reached.
And a number of bilateral agreements between Hong Kong and third countries on economic and legal issues such as investment protection were settled.
But as this week's talks represent the penultimate session before June 30, there remains much to resolve.
Davies said he had agreed some time ago with his Chinese counterpart that they would try to clear the whole JLG agenda by this week's meeting, but to no avail.
And in a clue to how tough the talks are, he told reporters: "I don't want to expose the differences between the British and Chinese sides in public. I don't think that would be helpful."
